item.title: Travel Vaccine Alert: CDC Warns of Polio Risk in 32 Countries Before Spring Break
item.description:
The last natural polio infection in the United States occurred in 1979. Most Americans have never thought twice about the disease. But on March 3, the CDC issued a Level 2 travel notice covering 32 countries — and some of the names on that list will surprise you.

Key Takeaways

  • The CDC issued a Level 2 travel notice on March 3 for polio, covering 32 countries
  • Advisory includes European nations like the UK, Spain, Finland, Germany, and Poland
  • Poliovirus is actively circulating in Africa, the Middle East, and parts of Europe
  • Adults who were vaccinated as children may need one lifetime booster shot before traveling
  • A separate measles surge is also fueling health warnings ahead of Spring Break
  • The inactivated polio vaccine is available at health departments and primary care offices

If you have international travel plans this spring, this is not something to scroll past. Here is everything you need to know.

item.title: MSP Airport Spring Break Chaos: TSA Wait Times, Staff Pressure, and What Travelers Need to Know
item.description:
Spring break 2026 is hitting MSP Airport hard. With thousands of travelers flooding Minneapolis-Saint Paul International, TSA employees are under mounting pressure — yet security lines keep moving. Here’s everything you need to know before heading to the airport.

Key Takeaways

  • Spring break travelers are packing MSP Airport, driving significant volume increases
  • TSA employees face growing pressure amid federal workforce uncertainty, but lines keep moving
  • Current TSA wait times at MSP remain manageable despite the surge
  • MSP also making headlines in managed service provider (MSP) industry with major deals

MSP Airport Spring Break Rush — What’s Happening on the Ground

According to KARE 11, spring break travelers are packing MSP Airport as of March 2026. The annual surge has turned terminals into a sea of families, college students, and vacationers all competing for overhead bin space.
